name: llama_decode_4c
purpose: The multi-core weight-streaming workload the project's scheduler/address-map investigations were run on, laid out realistically: 4 DMA cores splitting each layer of one model's weights.
description: 4 cores (core0.csv..core3.csv), 16 layers. Layer L's weights are one contiguous 1MB block at L*1MB; core c streams bytes [c*256KB, (c+1)*256KB) of it as 64 AXI reads of 4KB (size 64B x 64 beats, AXI id 1), then a BARRIER (its layer-L loads must land before its layer L+1 starts).

Scaled-down (16MB) version of the 1GB synthetic Llama-decode trace. That trace placed each core's buffer 4GB apart -- above bit 30, the highest bit this 2GB address map decodes -- so all four cores aliased onto the same banks/rows/columns and shared open rows: 70.4% utilization at 96.4% page-hit, describing a workload where four DMAs read the SAME weights. Here every address is inside the modeled capacity and high_address_regions must be 1.

Address map (from the bank-group-ordering fix): bankgroup [7:6] fastest-changing so consecutive 64B bursts pay tCCD_S not tCCD_L, then bank [9:8], channel [10], column [14:11], row [30:15]. A 4KB descriptor therefore sweeps all 32 banks twice (2 accesses per bank), and the next core's descriptor sweeps the same banks with a different row -- the inter-core row thrashing behind the ~50% conflict rate.

Known modeling limitation this case exposes (see bench/README.md): the scheduler starts every row miss's PRE/ACT only after the data bus is nearly free, instead of overlapping it with other banks' transfers as a real controller does, so each conflict exposes the full tRP+tRCD on the data bus. Expect this case to move sharply UP when that is fixed.
numbers_in_prose: Numbers quoted in description/sanity_checks are from the run at authoring time and are NOT kept in sync with the model; they explain the reasoning, not the current values. golden.json holds the current numbers. The reasoning is what should be re-checked when a value moves -- if it no longer holds, that is a finding.
rng: none -- pure arithmetic sequence, no randomness
sanity_checks: high_address_regions == 1 -- the layout bug this case exists to have fixed
full-scale (1GB) run with the same layout gives the same utilization (14.4%) and hit/conflict (46.7% / 49.8%) -- the scale-down doesn't change the behavior
